concepts.title: Bipolar World and Cold War
concepts.description: Bipolar World and Cold War — part of the chapter on The Cold War Era.
key_ideas: Core principles of bipolar world and cold war
Step-by-step problem solving for bipolar world and cold war
Real-world applications of bipolar world and cold war

concepts.title: The Cuban Missile Crisis (1962)
concepts.description: An analysis of the 1962 confrontation between the US and the USSR over Soviet ballistic missiles deployed in Cuba, often considered the high point of Cold War tensions.
key_ideas: Discovery of Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba by the USA
US naval blockade and the logic of brinkmanship
Resolution through diplomatic negotiation between Kennedy and Khrushchev
Establishment of the hotline communication link

concepts.title: Logic of Deterrence and Military Alliances
concepts.description: Exploration of the strategic military doctrines that prevented direct war and the formation of opposing alliance systems.
key_ideas: Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD) and the logic of deterrence
Formation of the Western Alliance (NATO)
Formation of the Eastern Alliance (Warsaw Pact)
Role of SEATO and CENTO in extending US influence

concepts.title: Arenas of the Cold War
concepts.description: Examination of specific geographical regions where the Cold War competition led to crises and proxy wars without escalating into a third world war.
key_ideas: Crisis points: Korea, Berlin, Congo, and Afghanistan
The concept of limited war versus total war
Role of the UN and Non-Aligned countries in mediation
Human and economic costs of proxy conflicts

concepts.title: The Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)
concepts.description: Study of the challenge to bipolarity posed by newly decolonized nations refusing to join either power bloc.
key_ideas: Founding leaders: Tito, Nehru, Nasser, Sukarno, and Nkrumah
Distinction between non-alignment, neutrality, and isolationism
The Belgrade Summit (1961)
NAM as a political platform for the 'Third World'

concepts.title: New International Economic Order (NIEO)
concepts.description: Analysis of the economic dimension of the Cold War where Least Developed Countries (LDCs) demanded a fairer global trading system.
key_ideas: UNCTAD report (1972): Towards a New Trade Policy for Development
Control over natural resources by LDCs
Access to Western markets and technology
Transition of NAM from political to economic advocacy

concepts.title: India's Role and Arms Control Treaties
concepts.description: Evaluation of India's foreign policy during the Cold War and the global efforts to limit nuclear proliferation.
key_ideas: India's policy of staying independent of alliances while engaging both blocs
Criticisms of India's stance (inconsistency and Treaty of Friendship with USSR)
Major Arms Control Treaties: LTBT, NPT, SALT, and START
Impact of the Cold War's end on India's global strategy

concepts.title: Collapse of Soviet Union
concepts.description: Collapse of Soviet Union — part of the chapter on The End of Bipolarity.
key_ideas: Core principles of collapse of soviet union
Step-by-step problem solving for collapse of soviet union
Real-world applications of collapse of soviet union

concepts.title: Features of the Soviet System
concepts.description: An examination of the political and economic structure of the USSR prior to its collapse, focusing on the role of the Communist Party and state-controlled economy.
key_ideas: Primacy of the state and the institution of the Communist Party
Absence of opposition parties and centralized planning
The concept of the 'Second World' and the Warsaw Pact

concepts.title: Gorbachev and the Disintegration
concepts.description: Analysis of the reform policies introduced by Mikhail Gorbachev and how they inadvertently accelerated the collapse of the Soviet Union.
key_ideas: Introduction of Perestroika (restructuring) and Glasnost (openness)
The loosening of administrative control and rise of nationalism
The 1991 coup and the shift of power to Boris Yeltsin

concepts.title: Consequences of Disintegration
concepts.description: Evaluation of the geopolitical shifts that occurred immediately following the fall of the USSR, marking the end of the Cold War era.
key_ideas: End of Cold War confrontations and ideological disputes
Shift in power relations leading to US hegemony (Unipolarity)
Emergence of new independent states in Eastern Europe and Central Asia

concepts.title: Shock Therapy in Post-Communist Regimes
concepts.description: A study of the painful economic transition model from an authoritarian socialist system to a democratic capitalist system influenced by the World Bank and IMF.
key_ideas: Total shift to capitalist economy and privatization of state assets
The 'Largest Garage Sale in History' and devaluation of currency (Ruble)
Loss of social welfare safety nets and rise of economic inequality

concepts.title: India and Post-Communist Countries
concepts.description: Exploration of India's foreign policy adjustments post-1991, specifically focusing on the continuity of strong relations with Russia.
key_ideas: Vision of a multipolar world order shared by India and Russia
Indo-Russian Strategic Agreement of 2001
Cooperation in defense, energy, and space research

concepts.title: US Dominance and Resistance
concepts.description: US Dominance and Resistance — part of the chapter on US Hegemony in World Politics.
key_ideas: Core principles of us dominance and resistance
Step-by-step problem solving for us dominance and resistance
Real-world applications of us dominance and resistance

concepts.title: The First Gulf War and the New World Order
concepts.description: Explores the emergence of US hegemony following the collapse of the Soviet Union, focusing on the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait and the subsequent US-led liberation.
key_ideas: The concept of the 'New World Order' introduced by George H.W. Bush.
Operation Desert Storm and the role of the UN coalition.
The technological gap demonstrated by 'Smart Bombs' and the computer war.

concepts.title: The Clinton Era: Focus on Soft Power
concepts.description: Examines US foreign policy during the Clinton administration, characterized by a focus on democratic promotion, climate change, and world trade, alongside selective military interventions.
key_ideas: Shift from hard politics to 'soft issues' like democracy and trade.
Operation Infinite Reach and missile attacks in Sudan and Afghanistan.
US military intervention in Yugoslavia (Kosovo) without UN authorization.

concepts.title: 9/11 and the Global War on Terror
concepts.description: Analyzes the dramatic shift in US foreign policy following the September 11 attacks, leading to the invasion of Afghanistan and the establishment of a global anti-terror framework.
key_ideas: The events of 9/11 and the launch of Operation Enduring Freedom.
The toppling of the Taliban regime and the hunt for Al-Qaeda.
Controversies surrounding Guantanamo Bay and the suspension of international law.

concepts.title: The Iraq Invasion: Operation Iraqi Freedom
concepts.description: Investigates the 2003 US invasion of Iraq, the bypassing of the UN mandate, and the geopolitical consequences of the 'Coalition of the Willing'.
key_ideas: The rationale of Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) and regime change.
The failure to find WMDs and the subsequent insurgency.
The political and humanitarian costs of the occupation.

concepts.title: Three Dimensions of Hegemony: Hard, Structural, and Soft
concepts.description: Deconstructs the theoretical framework of hegemony into military dominance (Hard), economic/internet control (Structural), and cultural influence (Soft).
key_ideas: Hard Power: Unmatched military capability and spending.
Structural Power: Control of SLOCs (Sea Lines of Communication) and the Internet.
Soft Power: Cultural dominance, 'McDonaldization', and manufacturing consent.

concepts.title: Constraints on US Power and India's Strategy
concepts.description: Evaluates the internal and external limits on US hegemony and formulates strategic options for countries like India to interact with a hegemon.
key_ideas: The three constraints: Institutional architecture, domestic public opinion, and NATO.
Strategic choices: Bandwagoning (benefiting from the system) vs. Hiding (staying aloof).
India's evolving relationship with the US in a post-Cold War era.

concepts.title: UN and Reforms
concepts.description: UN and Reforms — part of the chapter on International Organisations.
key_ideas: Core principles of un and reforms
Step-by-step problem solving for un and reforms
Real-world applications of un and reforms

concepts.title: Evolution and Structure of the UN
concepts.description: An overview of the historical transition from the League of Nations to the United Nations and a detailed look at the UN's principal organs.
key_ideas: Failure of the League of Nations and the founding of the UN in 1945
Functions of the General Assembly and the Security Council
Roles of the Secretariat, ICJ, and ECOSOC

concepts.title: Global Economic Organisations
concepts.description: Examination of major international economic institutions, their functions in the global economy, and the criticisms regarding their governance structures.
key_ideas: Role of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in financial stability
World Bank's focus on human development and agriculture
World Trade Organisation (WTO) and the rules of global trade

concepts.title: NGOs and Humanitarian Agencies
concepts.description: Introduction to non-governmental organizations and specialized agencies that operate alongside the UN to monitor rights and safety.
key_ideas: Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch as watchdogs
Role of the IAEA in nuclear safety
Distinction between IGOs and NGOs in global politics

concepts.title: India and the UN
concepts.description: Analysis of India's historical role in the UN, its contribution to peacekeeping, and its specific arguments for a permanent seat on the Security Council.
key_ideas: India's objective criteria for permanent membership (population, democracy, economy)
Role in UN Peacekeeping missions
Strategic interest in Security Council expansion

concepts.title: The UN in a Unipolar World
concepts.description: Critical assessment of the United Nations' effectiveness and relevance in a world dominated by a single superpower (US hegemony).
key_ideas: Influence of the US on UN funding and decisions
The UN as a platform for negotiation despite power imbalances
Relevance of the UN for the remaining 190+ nations

concepts.title: Traditional and Non-Traditional Security
concepts.description: Traditional and Non-Traditional Security — part of the chapter on Security in the Contemporary World.
key_ideas: Core principles of traditional and non-traditional security
Step-by-step problem solving for traditional and non-traditional security
Real-world applications of traditional and non-traditional security

concepts.title: Components of Traditional Security
concepts.description: Exploration of the specific methods states use to maintain traditional security, focusing on the logic of deterrence, defense, balance of power, and alliance building.
key_ideas: Deterrence involves preventing war by raising the costs for the attacker.
Balance of Power is maintained by building military strength or forming coalitions.
Alliance building formalizes collective defense against common threats.

concepts.title: New Sources of Threats
concepts.description: Analysis of emerging dangers that threaten human existence beyond military attacks, categorizing them under human security and global security frameworks.
key_ideas: Terrorism targets civilians to achieve political goals through fear.
Human rights violations, global poverty, and migration are intertwined security issues.
Health epidemics (like HIV-AIDS, COVID-19) are considered non-traditional security threats due to their rapid spread and impact.

concepts.title: Cooperative Security
concepts.description: Examination of why non-traditional threats require international collaboration rather than military force, and the role of international organizations and NGOs.
key_ideas: Military force is ineffective against threats like poverty, environmental degradation, or pandemics.
Cooperation can be bilateral, regional, continental, or global depending on the threat.
Involves diverse actors including international organizations (UN, WHO), NGOs, and businesses.

concepts.title: India's Security Strategy
concepts.description: Assessment of the four broad components comprising India's approach to national and international security challenges.
key_ideas: Strengthening military capabilities to protect territorial integrity.
Strengthening international norms and institutions to protect national interests.
Meeting internal security challenges posed by separatist movements.
Developing the economy to reduce poverty and inequality as a source of insecurity.

concepts.title: Political and Economic Globalisation
concepts.description: Political and Economic Globalisation — part of the chapter on Globalisation.
key_ideas: Core principles of political and economic globalisation
Step-by-step problem solving for political and economic globalisation
Real-world applications of political and economic globalisation

concepts.title: Causes of Globalisation
concepts.description: Exploration of the fundamental drivers of globalisation, specifically the role of technology and the movement of various elements across borders.
key_ideas: Technological advancements (telegraph, telephone, microchip) as catalysts
The concept of 'Global Village' and time-space compression
Four flows: Ideas, Capital, Commodities, and People

concepts.title: Cultural Consequences
concepts.description: Analysis of how globalisation impacts local cultures, examining the tension between a uniform global culture and the modification of culture by local influences.
key_ideas: Cultural Homogenisation and the rise of a uniform global culture (McDonaldisation)
Cultural Heterogenisation and the modification of external influences
The concept of 'Soft Power' and the dominance of Western values

concepts.title: India and Globalisation
concepts.description: Examination of India's historical engagement with global flows and the specific impact of the 1991 New Economic Policy reforms.
key_ideas: Historical context: India as a link in the Silk Route vs. Colonial exploitation
The shift from protectionism to the 1991 Economic Reforms (Liberalisation)
Impact on Indian industrial sectors and labor markets

concepts.title: Resistance to Globalisation
concepts.description: Critical evaluation of the arguments against globalisation from both the political Left and Right, and the role of international forums in organizing resistance.
key_ideas: Left-wing critiques: Economic inequality and state weakening
Right-wing critiques: Loss of traditional culture and national sovereignty
Role of the World Social Forum (WSF) and anti-globalisation movements
